complexity_scope.guarantee: Uniform deterministic upper; randomized per-instance success >=2/3 with uniform worst-case cap.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: cp,Cp depend only on p; logarithmic exponent 6(p-1) is conservative and not claimed optimal.

complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Upper: evaluated genuine outward-normal tangent certificate. Lower: any feasible output xhat satisfying r_tan(xhat)<=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: Q>=2, fixed p>=2; worst case over arbitrarily large finite d. Upper is dimension independent; lower dimension grows with budget.

map: Section 3.4 identifies Proposition 5.2 as the Taylor-model certified strong solver S_{2/(p+1),2}. Lemmas 6.2 and 7.1 supply exact/inexact block second-difference control; Theorem 8.1 converts S_{gamma,b} into A_{gamma/(1+gamma),b+4}; certified restart Lemma 5.3 adds two logarithmic powers. These are source-linked interfaces: their full Sections 4–8 proofs were not read or independently checked here.

Section 9 pp.23–24 starts gamma_0=2/(p+1), bS_0=2. For j=1,...,p-1, gamma_j=2/(p+1+2j), bA_j=6j, bS_j=6j+2. The input exponents obey (p-1)gamma_{j-1}<=2 and (3/2)(p-1)gamma_{j-1}>=1, with final-level equality in the latter. Exactly p-1 admissible boosts give gamma_{p-1}=2/(3p-1), logarithmic power 6(p-1). Taking R=D gives L_A(D,epsilon)=1+log(3+Q). This is finite induction using already constructed routines.

Section 9 p.24 and Algorithm 6 p.25 explain that nested regularizations add known affine terms, each nested jet uses one original-F query, and active ancestor counters charge every call. Caps include failed trials and final evaluated certificate checks. The valid distance promise R=D ensures success before the final cap. Appendix A.1 p.34 gives the known-affine-hull reduction and exact normal lift, with at most one evaluated-certificate query on a singleton domain.

Sections 10.1–10.3 pp.25–27 construct an exactly flat smooth gate and a shifted contraction on the public ball B_2^d(R). Lemma 10.2 verifies monotonicity, dimension-independent highest-derivative smoothness, ball invariance and r_tan=||F_V||, so boundary outward normals do not cancel the obstruction. Lemma 10.4 proves a hidden-final-coordinate lower threshold Lp R^p/[8 Bp 16^(p-1)(N+1)^((3p-1)/2)]. These are mapped source arguments, not a standalone extracted Hard Family.

Section 11.1 p.28 chooses each resisting direction orthogonal to earlier directions and queries, then the final direction orthogonal also to the arbitrary output. For d>=2N+2, exact gate flatness makes every returned full jet consistent with one fixed admissible operator; the hidden-slab bound applies.

Section 11.2 pp.29–30 samples the entire random frame before the run and conditions on an independent seed. Simulated truncated-response queries depend only on revealed directions and remain bounded on every transcript. Lemma 11.2 and a union bound under equation (11.2) control unrevealed correlations, including the output, without conditioning on prior success events. With probability >=1-delta the entire true transcript and output equal the simulated ones, and the hidden-slab obstruction holds. Averaging over frames gives one fixed instance with seed failure probability >=1-delta. Taking delta=1/4 contradicts per-instance success >=2/3 whenever the threshold exceeds epsilon.

Section 11.3 pp.30–31 first rules out zero queries using opposite constant operators on an interval. With R=D/2 and c_res,p=1/(2^p 8 Bp 16^(p-1)), successful budgets obey T>=max{1,(c_res,p Q)^alpha_p-1}>=0.5(c_res,p)^alpha_p Q^alpha_p. Deterministic algorithms are randomized algorithms ignoring their seed. Together with Section 9 this proves the displayed bracket as a source-linked argument.

assumptions: F is defined and C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X. For every x,y in X, <F(x)-F(y),x-y>>=0 and ||D^(p-1)F(x)-D^(p-1)F(y)||op<=Lp||x-y||. Lp is an available upper bound, not necessarily minimal. No separate bounds on lower derivatives or ||F|| and no fixed positive strong-monotonicity modulus are assumed.
One exact feasible order-p oracle call returns the complete jet (F(x),DF(x),...,D^(p-1)F(x)), including entire symmetric derivative tensors.

Let J_{p,d}=R^d times the product, for j=1,...,p-1, of spaces of symmetric j-linear maps (R^d)^j -> R^d. At fixed public input and budget N, H_0 is empty, x_t=phi_t(xi,H_{t-1}) in X, H_t appends (x_t,O_p^F(x_t)), and xhat=psi(xi,H_N) in X. Rules are measurable and defined on every history of the prescribed ambient dimensions, including simulated histories. The seed xi is independent of F; deterministic algorithms have singleton seed. Early stopping is padded with ignored feasible queries while retaining the saved output.

Queries may depend on the full preceding transcript. There is no span condition, tensor-update restriction or requirement that the output was queried. Family members may depend on public input but must work for all compatible unknown operators.

The budget is a uniform worst-case cap on actual original-F calls, not an expected stopping time. All nested original-F queries, failed trials and evaluated certificate checks count. A jet of F(z)+az+b costs exactly one original-F jet query plus known affine data.

Arbitrary measurable internal operations on the transcript and known domain are permitted, including exact projections and exact solutions of known regularized Taylor-model VIs. They do not evaluate unknown F at unqueried points. Polynomial arithmetic/bit complexity and a free resolvent of unknown F are not assumed.
statement.conclusion: cp Q^{alpha_p} <= Trand_p(epsilon;Lp,D) <= Tdet_p(epsilon;Lp,D) <= Cp(1+Q^{alpha_p})[1+log(3+Q)]^{6(p-1)}, alpha_p=2/(3p-1). The upper method returns an explicit evaluated certificate (x,n,F(x)) with x in X, n in N_X(x) and ||F(x)+n||<=epsilon; its query bound is independent of d. Against an N-query method, the deterministic lower construction works for d>=2N+2. For randomized lower bounds d=O(N^3 log(N+2)) suffices at fixed failure probability. More precisely Section 11.2 takes m=N+1 and d>=m+ceil(2048m^3 log(2(m^2+1)/delta)), with delta=1/4 for the obstruction to per-instance success 2/3. These are high-dimensional worst-case lower bounds with bounded feasible queries and arbitrary feasible outputs, including unqueried outputs.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For fixed integer p>=2, public input is (d,X,x0,p,Lp,D,epsilon): finite d>=1, known nonempty compact convex X subset R^d, diam(X)<=D and x0 in X. Norms are Euclidean; for j-linear T, ||T||op=sup_{||u_i||<=1}||T[u_1,...,u_j]||. N_X(x)={n:<n,z-x><=0 for every z in X} is the outward normal cone. For feasible x, r_tan(x)=dist(0,F(x)+N_X(x))=inf_{n in N_X(x)}||F(x)+n||. Tdet_p(epsilon;Lp,D) is the least N in N_0 for which a deterministic algorithm family succeeds for every finite dimension, admissible public domain/initial point, and compatible unknown F; it is +infinity if no finite budget works. Trand_p is analogous with success probability at least 2/3 for each individual F. Q=Lp D^p/epsilon and alpha_p=2/(3p-1).
statement.parameter_domains: Fixed integer p>=2; Lp,D,epsilon>0; Q>=2. Finite d>=1, unbounded in the worst case. Lower construction budgets N>=1; the zero-query case is handled separately. Constants are not uniform as p tends to infinity.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed integer p>=2 there exist positive cp,Cp depending only on p such that for all Lp,D,epsilon>0 with Q>=2 the conclusion holds. Complexity is uniform over arbitrarily large finite dimensions and admissible public inputs. For every fixed compatible F, randomized success is P_xi{r_tan(xhat)<=epsilon}>=2/3 under a worst-case call cap. A hard instance may depend on the algorithm but is fixed independently of its seed; this is not average-instance success.
